description: DB integration: a scheduled comment (publish_state='scheduled') is EXCLUDED from the client-portal read path (client-tickets.ts conversations query) against migrated schema
DB integration: a scheduled comment is EXCLUDED from the REST API TicketService.getTicketComments client-visibility branch, including across pagination boundaries (short page cannot leak)
Integration: scheduling a client-visible comment dispatches NO client notification and does NOT advance response_state at schedule time (event suppressed)
Integration: at/after scheduled_publish_at the publish handler transitions to published, the comment becomes visible on both client-facing read paths, and response_state advances
Integration (idempotency): running the publish handler twice for the same comment (retry) emits TICKET_COMMENT_ADDED exactly once (second run matches 0 rows, no event)
Integration (restart/overdue): boot reconciler publishes an overdue scheduled comment exactly once and re-arms a future one without duplicating the notification
Integration (permissions guard): scheduling is rejected for a client author, for an internal-only comment, and for a past timestamp
Integration (cancel): cancel sets publish_state='canceled', soft-withdraws, prevents publication (handler guard) so the client never sees it and no notification fires; audit + author preserved
Integration (reschedule): reschedule cancels the prior job, arms a new one, updates scheduled_publish_at, and publishes only at the new time
Integration (edit while scheduled): editing a scheduled comment's content keeps it invisible to clients and does not change the schedule or trigger a notification
Integration (tenant/timezone safety): publish job carries tenantId and stays tenant-scoped; scheduled_publish_at stored as UTC while scheduled_publish_tz preserves the originating IANA zone

E2E (MSP UI): agent schedules a client-visible comment; it appears in Client/All tabs with a Scheduled badge + publish timestamp/zone and Edit/Reschedule/Cancel actions; client portal shows nothing until publish
Regression: an immediate (unscheduled) client-visible comment and an internal-only comment behave exactly as before (immediate visibility/notification; internal stays hidden)

Component behavior: the default bento timeline client composer resolves a datetime-local value in the user time zone and forwards it as the fifth schedule argument; leaving an invalid schedule for internal/resolution forwards null and remains submittable; cancel/reopen clears scheduling state
